---
title: "Snakemake-ify"
description: "Ten exercises: turn the lab's old analysis scripts into Snakemake rules, one script at a time, then the whole chain."
---

Most pipelines in a lab start as a folder of scripts and a `run_all.sh`. This
page gives you such a folder, written the way people really write them, and
asks you to convert it to Snakemake one script at a time. The scripts run on
the course data and they work. Each one also has a habit that Snakemake
replaces, and a few have problems that only show up when something goes wrong.

The exercises go from easy to hard. Do them in order: each one builds on the
rules from the one before. The last exercise puts everything into one
Snakefile.

::: {.callout-note}
## Before you start

- The course environment (`conda activate snakemake-course`, see [Setup](../setup.qmd)).
- Modules 1-4. Exercises 6, 8 and 9 use `script:` (module 6), so you may want to do those after day 2.
- About 10 minutes per exercise, 30 for the last one.
:::

## Setup

All the scripts are in [`snakemakeify/`](../snakemakeify/README.md) in the course
repository. Make one working folder for these exercises, with a link to the
course data and a subfolder for the legacy run:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/snakemakeify/legacy
cd ~/snakemakeify
ln -s ~/snakemake-course/data data
```

Each script has `DATA=~/snakemake-course/data` at the top. If your copy of the
course is somewhere else, change that line in each script (you will see why
that is annoying). Then run the whole legacy analysis once:

```bash
cd ~/snakemakeify/legacy
bash ~/snakemake-course/snakemakeify/run_all.sh 2>&1 | tee run_all.log
```

It takes about a minute and a half on a 4-core machine. Keep `legacy/`: every
exercise compares your outputs with it.

Write your Snakefiles in `~/snakemakeify/` (one per exercise, for example
`ex1.smk`, run with `snakemake -s ex1.smk -c 4`), and send outputs to a
`results/` folder. The checks below use the paths from the answer key; adjust
them if you named things differently. Our solutions live in
`answers/snakemakeify/` and run from the same folder:

```bash
cd ~/snakemakeify
snakemake -s ~/snakemake-course/answers/snakemakeify/ex1.smk -c 4
```

## S1. FastQC {#ex-s1-q}

::: {.callout-tip .exercise}
## Exercise S1: FastQC

```{.bash filename="snakemakeify/01_fastqc.sh"}
{{< include ../snakemakeify/01_fastqc.sh >}}
```

**Goal.** One rule, `fastqc`, that runs FastQC on one sample, and a `rule all`
that asks for every sample.

**Watch for.**

- The `for` loop and the `if [ -f ... ]` check. Snakemake does both for you.
  What replaces the sample list?
- FastQC names its outputs itself, from the input file name. Your `output:`
  has to match what it writes, or Snakemake reports missing output files.
- FastQC writes two files per sample. Declare both.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Hint

The output folder is a fixed argument (`--outdir results/fastqc`), so the
rule's output paths are `results/fastqc/{sample}_fastqc.html` and
`results/fastqc/{sample}_fastqc.zip`. Build the sample list from
`data/samplesheet.txt` with pandas (module 3) instead of typing it.
:::

**Done when**

- `snakemake -s ex1.smk -n` shows 11 jobs: 10 `fastqc` and `all`.
- The FastQC results match the legacy ones (the HTML has a date in it, so
  compare the report data inside the zip):

  ```bash
  s=HCT116_CTCF_1
  diff <(unzip -p legacy/fastqc/${s}_fastqc.zip ${s}_fastqc/fastqc_data.txt) \
       <(unzip -p results/fastqc/${s}_fastqc.zip ${s}_fastqc/fastqc_data.txt) && echo same
  ```

[Answer](../answers/snakemakeify-answers.qmd#ex-s1)
:::

## S2. Index and align {#ex-s2-q}

::: {.callout-tip .exercise}
## Exercise S2: Index and align

```{.bash filename="snakemakeify/02_align.sh"}
{{< include ../snakemakeify/02_align.sh >}}
```

**Goal.** Rules that unzip the reference, build the bowtie2 index once, and
align each sample.

**Watch for.**

- The index is built "only if `chr8_course.1.bt2` is missing". bowtie2 writes
  six index files. Try it in an empty folder: copy only `chr8_course.1.bt2`
  from `legacy/` and run `02_align.sh`. The index is not rebuilt, every
  alignment fails, and the script still exits with status 0. What would
  Snakemake do if one of six declared outputs were missing?
- `samtools faidx` is there "for later". Nothing says which later step uses it.
  Give it a rule with a declared output, so the step that needs it can ask for it.
- `bowtie2 ... | samtools sort`: without `set -o pipefail`, a failed bowtie2
  is invisible to the script. Snakemake runs shell commands in strict mode
  (`set -euo pipefail`).
- `THREADS=4` becomes `threads:`.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Hint

`multiext("results/index/chr8_course", ".1.bt2", ".2.bt2", ".3.bt2", ".4.bt2", ".rev.1.bt2", ".rev.2.bt2")`
lists all six index files in one line. bowtie2 wants the prefix, not a file
name: pass it with `params:`.
:::

**Done when**

- `snakemake -s ex2.smk -n` shows 13 jobs: `reference`, `bowtie2_index`, 10 `align`, `all`.
- Each BAM has the same number of records as the legacy one, for example 28634
  for HCT116_CTCF_1:

  ```bash
  for s in $(cut -f2,4,5 data/samplesheet.txt | tail -n +2 | tr '\t' '_'); do
      echo $s $(samtools view -c legacy/$s.bam) $(samtools view -c results/align/$s.bam)
  done
  ```

  The BAM files are not byte-for-byte identical, and that is expected: with
  `-p 4`, bowtie2 writes reads in the order its threads finish, so reads at the
  same position can come out in a different order.

[Answer](../answers/snakemakeify-answers.qmd#ex-s2)
:::

## S3. One script, many outputs {#ex-s3-q}

::: {.callout-tip .exercise}
## Exercise S3: One script, many outputs

```{.bash filename="snakemakeify/03_filter.sh"}
{{< include ../snakemakeify/03_filter.sh >}}
```

**Goal.** Split this script into rules: filtering, duplicate removal,
flagstat and bigWig.

**Watch for.**

- The script writes six files per sample. Which of them does a later step
  need? Each group of files that comes from one command is one rule.
- The skip check only looks at `$s.filt.bam`. If `bamCoverage` failed for a
  sample, the next run skips that sample and the bigWig never appears.
- The `rm` at the end of the loop. What does `temp()` do instead?
- `MAPQ=30`, the bin size and the read extension are settings. Move them to a
  config file and pass them with `params:`.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Hint

Pipe `samtools view -q` into `bedtools intersect -v -abam stdin` in one rule
and mark its output `temp()`. `samtools markdup -r` and `samtools index` go
in a second rule with two outputs (`.filt.bam` and `.filt.bam.bai`), and
`bamCoverage` should take the `.bai` as an input even though it is not on its
command line.
:::

**Done when**

- In a fresh folder, `snakemake -s ex3.smk -n` shows 53 jobs (13 from S2 plus
  10 each of `filter_reads`, `markdup`, `flagstat`, `bigwig`).
- The flagstat files and the bigWigs are byte-for-byte identical to the legacy ones:

  ```bash
  for f in legacy/*.flagstat.txt; do cmp $f results/filter/$(basename $f); done
  for f in legacy/tracks/*.bw; do cmp $f results/tracks/$(basename $f); done
  ```

  No output means no differences. HCT116_CTCF_1 keeps 24453 reads.
- After the run, `results/filter/` has no `.noBL.bam` files.

[Answer](../answers/snakemakeify-answers.qmd#ex-s3)
:::

## S4. Peaks with a control {#ex-s4-q}

::: {.callout-tip .exercise}
## Exercise S4: Peaks with a control

```{.bash filename="snakemakeify/04_call_peaks.sh"}
{{< include ../snakemakeify/04_call_peaks.sh >}}
```

**Goal.** One `call_peaks` rule that works for ChIP samples (with their
control) and for DNase (no control).

**Watch for.**

- The control is looked up by name in the samplesheet, inside a `while read`
  loop. In Snakemake this is an input function: given `wildcards.sample`, return
  the treatment BAM and, if there is one, the control BAM.
- The DNase branch has different MACS3 options. That is a `params:` value that
  depends on the sample.
- Which samples get peaks? The script skips any target starting with `input`.
  Is that rule written down anywhere else?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Hint

Return a dict from the input function and wrap it in `unpack()`, so you get
`input.treatment` and, for ChIP only, `input.control`. A params function can
take `(wildcards, input)` and check `"control" in input.keys()`.
:::

**Done when**

- `snakemake -s ex4.smk -n` (fresh folder) shows 39 jobs, 6 of them `call_peaks`.
- All six peak files and summit files are byte-for-byte identical:

  ```bash
  for f in legacy/peaks/*_peaks.narrowPeak legacy/peaks/*_summits.bed; do
      cmp $f results/peaks/$(basename $f)
  done
  wc -l results/peaks/*_peaks.narrowPeak
  ```

  You should see 24 and 64 CTCF peaks, 138 and 141 H3K27ac, 223 and 217 DNase.

[Answer](../answers/snakemakeify-answers.qmd#ex-s4)
:::

## S5. A parameter sweep {#ex-s5-q}

::: {.callout-tip .exercise}
## Exercise S5: A parameter sweep

```{.bash filename="snakemakeify/05_qvalue_sweep.sh"}
{{< include ../snakemakeify/05_qvalue_sweep.sh >}}
```

**Goal.** Make the q-value a wildcard, so one rule makes every
`{sample}_q{q}` peak file, and a second rule builds the table from them.

**Watch for.**

- The two loops (samples, q-values) become one `expand()` with two lists.
- `CONTROL=HCT116_input-CTCF_1` is used for both replicates. Check the
  samplesheet. Then compare the `q 0.01` row for HCT116_CTCF_2 in
  `legacy/sweep/sweep_counts.tsv` with its peak count from S4.
- Put the q-values in the config as strings, so the file names use exactly
  the text you typed. As numbers they go through Python's `str()`: try
  `str(0.00001)` and `str(0.050)`.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Hint

`output: "results/sweep/{sample}_q{q}_peaks.narrowPeak"` and
`-q {wildcards.q}` in the command. Reuse the samplesheet lookup from S4 for the
control. The table can be a short `run:` block that loops over `input`.
:::

**Done when**

- `snakemake -s ex5.smk -n` (fresh folder) shows 24 jobs: 8 `sweep_call` and one
  `sweep_counts`, plus the alignment and filtering for the two CTCF samples and
  their two controls only.
- `diff legacy/sweep/sweep_counts.tsv results/sweep/sweep_counts.tsv` shows the
  four HCT116_CTCF_1 rows the same and the four HCT116_CTCF_2 rows different
  (legacy 66, 62, 57, 54; yours 67, 64, 60, 55). Your `q 0.01` row for
  HCT116_CTCF_2 now agrees with the 64 peaks from S4. Explain the difference
  in one sentence.

[Answer](../answers/snakemakeify-answers.qmd#ex-s5)
:::

## S6. A Python script that globs {#ex-s6-q}

::: {.callout-tip .exercise}
## Exercise S6: A Python script that globs

```{.python filename="snakemakeify/06_qc_summary.py"}
{{< include ../snakemakeify/06_qc_summary.py >}}
```

**Goal.** Run this script from a rule with `script:`, with every file name
coming from the rule.

**Watch for.**

- `glob("*.filt.bam")` means "whatever happens to be in the folder". Snakemake
  needs to know the inputs before it runs anything.
- `if os.path.exists(peaks) ... else "NA"`: if peak calling failed or has not
  run yet, the script writes NA and exits happily. Try it: in a copy of
  `legacy/` delete `peaks/HCT116_CTCF_1_peaks.narrowPeak` and run the script.
  In your rule, the peak files are inputs, so a missing one stops the rule.
- How does the script know which peak file belongs to which sample once there
  is no glob? Pass the sample names in `params:`.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Hint

Three named inputs built with `expand()`: `bams`, `flagstats` (all samples)
and `peaks` (only samples that get peaks). In the script,
`dict(zip(snakemake.params.peak_samples, snakemake.input.peaks))` gives you
the lookup. Sort the rows by sample name so the table matches the legacy one.
:::

**Done when**

- `snakemake -s ex6.smk -n` (fresh folder) shows 50 jobs.
- `cmp legacy/qc_summary.tsv results/qc/qc_summary.tsv` prints nothing.

[Answer](../answers/snakemakeify-answers.qmd#ex-s6)
:::

## S7. Overlaps and a file that lies {#ex-s7-q}

::: {.callout-tip .exercise}
## Exercise S7: Overlaps and a file that lies

```{.bash filename="snakemakeify/07_overlap.sh"}
{{< include ../snakemakeify/07_overlap.sh >}}
```

**Goal.** A `consensus_peaks` rule with a `{target}` wildcard, plus rules for
the RAD21 overlap, the summit windows and the counts.

**Watch for.**

- `chr8_course.fa.fai` comes from `02_align.sh`, as a side effect. Nothing in
  this script says so. Run it in a folder without that file and the summit step fails.
- Run this in an empty folder before any peaks exist:

  ```bash
  mkdir ~/snakemakeify/bug && cd ~/snakemakeify/bug
  bash ~/snakemake-course/snakemakeify/07_overlap.sh
  cp -r ../legacy/peaks ../legacy/chr8_course.fa.fai .
  bash ~/snakemake-course/snakemakeify/07_overlap.sh
  ```

  Both runs report 0 lines in every file. `> file` creates the file before
  bedtools fails, and the skip check then treats that empty file as finished
  work. Snakemake removes the outputs of a job that fails, and it would not
  run this step before its inputs exist.
- The targets and the "rep 1 vs rep 2" pairing are typed in. Get the replicates
  of a target from the samplesheet.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Hint

An input function `lambda wc: expand("results/peaks/{sample}_peaks.narrowPeak", sample=reps_of(wc.target))`,
where `reps_of()` reads the samplesheet. The `.fai` should be an output of the
reference rule from S2 and an input here.
:::

**Done when**

- `snakemake -s ex7.smk -n` (fresh folder) shows 45 jobs, 3 of them `consensus_peaks`.
- All five BED files are byte-for-byte identical to the legacy ones
  (`for f in legacy/overlap/*.bed; do cmp $f results/overlap/$(basename $f); done`).
  The CTCF consensus has 24 peaks, 19 of them with RAD21.

[Answer](../answers/snakemakeify-answers.qmd#ex-s7)
:::

## S8. An R figure with hard-coded files {#ex-s8-q}

::: {.callout-tip .exercise}
## Exercise S8: An R figure with hard-coded files

```{.r filename="snakemakeify/08_locus_plot.R"}
{{< include ../snakemakeify/08_locus_plot.R >}}
```

**Goal.** Run this from a `locus_plot` rule with `script:`. Every file name and
the region come from `snakemake@input`, `snakemake@params` and `snakemake@output`.

**Watch for.**

- The bigWig list, the peak list and the labels are typed in. Add a sample and
  the figure silently leaves it out.
- The region is three numbers in the code. It belongs in the config.
- R messages go to the terminal. Send them to a `log:` file with `sink()`.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Hint

Named inputs come through as `snakemake@input$bigwigs` (a list). `unlist()` it
and name it with `setNames(..., unlist(snakemake@params$track_names))`.
:::

**Done when**

- `snakemake -s ex8.smk -n` (fresh folder) shows 49 jobs. Only the six
  peak-calling samples need a bigWig here.
- `cmp legacy/MYC_locus_CTCF_peaks.tsv results/figures/MYC_locus_CTCF_peaks.tsv`
  prints nothing, and `results/figures/MYC_locus.pdf` shows six tracks and four
  peak rows (CTCF, H3K27ac, DNase, RAD21), like the legacy PDF.

[Answer](../answers/snakemakeify-answers.qmd#ex-s8)
:::

## S9. TT-seq over enhancers {#ex-s9-q}

::: {.callout-tip .exercise}
## Exercise S9: TT-seq over enhancers

```{.r filename="snakemakeify/09_ttseq_enhancers.R"}
{{< include ../snakemakeify/09_ttseq_enhancers.R >}}
```

This one uses the processed TT-seq data from GEO (GSE152291) in `data/geo/`:
strand-specific bigWigs for two replicates, and the authors' HCT116 enhancer
annotation.

**Goal.** One rule with `{rep}` and `{strand}` wildcards that computes the
signal for one bigWig, and one rule that joins them into the per-replicate
tables and the combined table.

**Watch for.**

- Two nested loops over values that are typed in (`c(1, 2)`,
  `c("plus", "minus")`). They become two wildcards and two config lists.
- The bigWig file name is built with `paste0()`. In Snakemake it is a pattern
  in the config: `geo/TTseq_HCT116_{rep}_{strand}.bw`.
- `cov[["chr8"]]` assumes one chromosome.
- One script writes three tables. With one job per bigWig, the four signal jobs
  can run at the same time.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Hint

An output can be an `expand()`:
`reps=expand("results/ttseq/ttseq_enhancers_rep{rep}.tsv", rep=config["ttseq"]["reps"])`.
In R that is `snakemake@output$reps`, a list in the same order.
:::

**Done when**

- `snakemake -s ex9.smk -n` shows 6 jobs: 4 `ttseq_signal`, `ttseq_tables`, `all`.
- The three tables (118 enhancers each) are byte-for-byte identical:

  ```bash
  for f in legacy/ttseq_enhancers_*.tsv; do cmp $f results/ttseq/$(basename $f); done
  ```

[Answer](../answers/snakemakeify-answers.qmd#ex-s9)
:::

## S10. The whole of run_all.sh {#ex-s10-q}

::: {.callout-tip .exercise}
## Exercise S10: The whole of run_all.sh

```{.bash filename="snakemakeify/run_all.sh"}
{{< include ../snakemakeify/run_all.sh >}}
```

**Goal.** One Snakefile with every rule from S1-S9, one config file, and a
`rule all` that asks for the final outputs. No `run_all.sh`.

**Watch for.**

- The order of the steps in `run_all.sh` is now the DAG's job. You do not write
  it down anywhere.
- `run_all.sh` does not stop when a step fails, and re-running it redoes 06,
  08 and 09 every time (about 20 seconds of work for nothing). Snakemake reruns
  only what is out of date.
- What is the smallest `rule all`? You only need to list the ends of the chains.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Hint

List the FastQC reports, the bigWigs, `qc_summary.tsv`, `sweep_counts.tsv`,
`overlap/counts.txt`, the PDF and `ttseq_enhancers_all.tsv`. Everything else
is pulled in. Then draw it: `snakemake -s Snakefile --dag | dot -Tpdf > dag.pdf`.
:::

**Done when**

- `snakemake -n` in a fresh folder shows 91 jobs.
- The real run (`-c 4`) finishes; ours took 74 seconds on 4 cores.
- A second `snakemake -n` says `Nothing to be done`.
- `touch results/filter/HCT116_CTCF_1.filt.bam`, then `snakemake -n`: 15 jobs,
  only the ones downstream of that file.
- Every check from S1-S9 still holds.

[Answer](../answers/snakemakeify-answers.qmd#ex-s10)
:::

analyses, in the lab's pipeline layout.
